problem:
Arranged in **ascending order**, the solutions of the equation $\operatorname{cos}⁡x=-\frac{1}{2}$ for $-\pi <x\le \pi $ are $x=${{field-1}} and $x=$
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{1}{2})=\frac{2\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\frac{2\pi }{3}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is $x=\frac{2\pi }{3}.$

Our first solution lies in the second quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{3}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{3}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14061537/assets/a22dba264faa711352724f135d2ec5a074202c4b5069dee2389fe954419a3770.png)

A second solution $X$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, and we can find it using the reference angle, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{4\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

However, this value is not in the required domain. To get a second solution that's within the required domain, we simply subtract $2\pi $ from $X:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =X-2\pi  \\  & =\frac{4\pi }{3}-2\pi  \\  & =-\frac{2\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, arranged in ascending order, the solutions are $x=-\frac{2\pi }{3}$ and $x=\frac{2\pi }{3}.$
